messages:
Lara (platform): heads-up — I prototyped a new canary failover pattern i’m calling ‘surge-absorber’. idea: instead of immediate rollback when capacity blips, route canary traffic to a cheaper, compatible variant while we heal infra :thinking_face:
Mike (eng-platform): love the name. short Q: is this for transient GPU OOMs only or also for regional network flaps?
Lara (platform): both. policy has three lanes: primary (canary model), absorber (smaller/quantized variant), and fallback (stable prod). we drain to absorber first, then fallback if errors persist.
Anika (eng-sre): need hard guardrails. prefer automatic only for latency spikes and OOMs. for model-quality regressions (hallucination, rouge drop) we should alert but not auto-swap.
James (eng-runtime): agreed. runtime can detect OOM / enqueue growth / qps saturation. for model-quality we can use eval hooks to mark signals.
Mike (eng-platform): UX question — how does console expose this? i imagine a canary config with JSON-ish policy. example:
```json
{
  "traffic_split": 0.05,
  "safety_window": 300,
  "absorber": {
    "model": "gpt-small-q4",
    "max_duration": 180
  },
  "triggers": {
    "latency_p95_ms": 2000,
    "error_rate_pct": 1.0,
    "oom_detected": true
  },
  "rollback_policy": "sequential"
}
```
Lara (platform): that maps to the runtime. safety_window is the stabilisation period before auto-swap allowed. max_duration is how long absorber stays on before full fallback.
Anika (eng-sre): telemetry: we need histograms (p50/p95/p99), enqueue depth, kv-cache-miss-rate, and model quality drift (baseline compare). also add a circuit-breaker cooldown to prevent flip-flopping.
James (eng-runtime): we can implement a cooldown token bucket per route. if absorber engages, lock swaps for cooldown_secs to avoid thrash. also attach trace id to every swapped request for postmortem.
Lara (platform): question for infra — when absorber is chosen, do we route in-region only or allow cross-region absorption? cross-region can increase latency but keeps availability. thoughts?
Anika (eng-sre): prefer in-region first, then cross-region if capacity shortage persists >2min. set a max added latency budget.
Mike (eng-platform): console UX: show live mini-graph for canary lane: traffic %, absorber count, cooldown countdown, and one-click promote/rollback. also make the triggers editable with presets: conservative/normal/aggressive.
James (eng-runtime): implementation notes: runtime needs composite routing rules: priority+weight+predicate. predicate examples: oom==true, p95>threshold, enqueue>threshold. when predicate true => switch to absorber with weight 100 for canary sessions only. persistent failure => escalate to fallback for all traffic.
Lara (platform): i want an option to auto-notify the is-team and the owning PM on absorber engagement, with quick reason tags (OOM, latency, quality-drift).
DeployBot: Canary started: id=canary-2027-04-14-7f3a, traffic=5%, region=us-west-2
Mike (eng-platform): nice. can we run a small simulation first? feed synthetic latency spikes and verify absorber engages and cooldown behaves.
James (eng-runtime): yes, i’ll add a test harness that feeds enqueue pressure and OOM signals. plan: unit tests + chaos run in staging.
Anika (eng-sre): we should also add a post-engagement eval job that computes model divergence score over recent requests and stores to telemetry so PMs can inspect quality impact of absorber vs fallback.
Lara (platform): outcome: i’ll draft a spec with the JSON schema + ui mockups + proposed defaults (safety_window=5min, cooldown=3min, absorber_max=3min). assign owners?
Mike (eng-platform): i’ll do console mocks.
James (eng-runtime): i’ll do runtime rules and test harness.
Anika (eng-sre): i'll own telemetry and alerting thresholds.
Lara (platform): thanks — will post spec in #design later. :thumbsup:
DeployBot: Canary update: id=canary-2027-04-14-7f3a, status=absorber_engaged, reason=oom_detected, started_at=1918475700
Mike (eng-platform): saw the notification. absorber holding at gpt-small-q4, traffic still 5%. logs show enqueue depth spiking then decrementing.
James (eng-runtime): runtime comment — absorber engaged for canary session sticky routing only, not global swap. cooldown timer started.
Anika (eng-sre): monitoring shows p95 dropped after absorber, no errors. marking incident = no. recommend postmortem note about capacity tuning.
Lara (platform): perfect — this is the kind of graceful degradation we wanted. will iterate on thresholds after we collect a few canary runs.
